title: How Many Samples Are Needed to Determine Causal Direction? Sharp Minimax Bounds for Bivariate LiNGAM
abstract:
arXiv:2608.15840v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study how many observations are needed to determine the causal direction between two linearly related variables. Classical LiNGAM theory shows that independent non-Gaussian disturbances identify the direction, but does not quantify the difficulty when the causal effect is weak or the disturbances are nearly Gaussian. translated_title: 确定因果方向需要多少样本？双变量LiNGAM的尖锐极小极大界
translated_abstract:
arXiv:2608.15840v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：我们研究了确定两个线性相关变量之间的因果方向需要多少观测值。经典LiNGAM理论表明，独立的非高斯扰动可以识别方向，但当因果效应较弱或扰动接近高斯分布时，并未量化难度。设$ eta$为结构系数绝对值的下界，$
u$衡量每个标准化扰动与高斯分布的距离，并设扰动尺度位于$[\underline\sigma,\overline\sigma]$范围内。我们证明了尖锐的局部极小极大律 \[   N_2^\star( eta,
u,\delta)   \asymp    rac{\log(1/\delta)}   {d_ eta^2+ eta^2
u^2},   \qquad   d_ eta=   \left[ eta^2  \left(1- rac{\underline\sigma^2}{\overline\sigma^2}ight)ight]_+. \] 以往理论建立了总体可识别性或假设两个方向之间存在固定分离。相比之下，我们建立了尖锐的样本复杂度。
tldr: 本文首次给出了双变量LiNGAM中确定因果方向所需样本数的尖锐极小极大下界，揭示了因果效应强度、非高斯性和扰动尺度差异如何共同决定样本复杂度。
en_tdlr: This paper provides the first sharp minimax lower bound on the sample complexity for determining causal direction in bivariate LiNGAM, revealing how causal effect strength, non-Gaussianity, and disturbance scale differences jointly determine the required sample size.
